config.experiment: M1C.1 — fixed-uniform kernel ablation (A vs U vs B): isolating near-bias from deficit-unawareness
config.research_question: If the M1 selection rule remains unchanged and redistribution remains fixed and deficit-unaware, does removing the near-bias eliminate or substantially weaken churn?
config.motivation: M1C changed several properties of the redistribution law at once (fixed near-biased q -> adaptive target-aware oracle), so it cannot tell whether churn is driven by (1) the near-bias/target mismatch of the fixed law, (2) the law being fixed and deficit-unaware, or (3) both. Variant U is the missing middle control: still fixed, state-unaware and deficit-unaware, but the fixed law equals the uniform target.

variants.A: canonical M1A/M1B baseline, untouched: initial state q_near, removed mass resprayed with fixed q_near (redistribution='throw', redistribution_dist=None)
variants.U: selection identical; initial state identical (q_near); removed mass resprayed with the fixed uniform law q_uniform[i] = 1/K (redistribution='throw', redistribution_dist=uniform). Still fixed, state-unaware, deficit-unaware; only the near-bias is removed.
variants.B: existing M1C oracle control, unchanged: selection identical; removed mass redistributed by target-aware deficit filling (redistribution='deficit_fill')

controlled_variable_logic.A_vs_U: fixed + deficit-unaware + near-biased  vs  fixed + deficit-unaware + uniform  -> isolates near-bias / target mismatch
controlled_variable_logic.U_vs_B: fixed uniform + deficit-unaware  vs  adaptive deficit-aware oracle  -> isolates state/deficit awareness
controlled_variable_logic.caveat: this factor table is a device for mechanism interpretation; it does not prove the properties are independently manipulable in general

config.initial_state: q_near bin probabilities (identical for A, U and B)
config.throw_distribution_A: q_near(x) = 2(1-x); respray law of Variant A and the shared initial condition
config.redistribution_law_U: q_uniform[i] = 1/K on the same K-bin grid, exact CDF differencing; fixed, state-unaware, deficit-unaware
invariants: mass conservation: sum(p_next) == sum(p_current) within float tolerance
non-negativity: no bin mass below zero
exact uniform law: q_uniform[i] = 1/K within 1e-15 and sum = 1
selection invariance: same current state -> same cumulative excess, boundary, selected region and removed mass for A/U/B (trajectories may diverge only after divergent updates)
U update identity: the per-round added mass is exactly M_removed / K in every bin (constant vector)
config.diagnostics: same metrics and churn diagnostics as M1B.2/M1C: U_density, D_max, sweep boundary, moved mass, cumulative moved mass, L1 step, exact stopping time, epsilon first-passage, best-uniformity time/value, retention, late-stage behaviour, increasing-D_max / worsening-U step shares
config.late_stage_definition: active rounds with D_max < 0.005 (M1B.2 convention), plus last-25%-of-active-rounds window
config.baseline_policy: re-run A and B under the frozen configuration and string-compare key summary fields against the committed M1C results; stop before interpretation on any mismatch
config.no_post_hoc_tuning: frozen kernel set {q_near, q_uniform, deficit-fill}; no interpolation, no alpha/K/epsilon changes, no mixed or adaptive laws; results accepted as-is
config.mc_path_scope: deterministic expected-mass path only (as in M1C); all Stage-1 churn evidence lives on that path
